## What changed

**The packages come from a different host than the indexes, and the proxy only
covered one of them.** `packages.gitlab.com` serves `InRelease`, `Release` and
`Packages.gz` itself, but hands out every `.deb` as a redirect to Google
Storage — checked on 13.12.15, 14.0.12, 16.3.9, 17.11.7 and 18.11.11, all five
land on `storage.googleapis.com`. A proxy configured for
`packages.gitlab.com` alone therefore covers `apt-get update` and covers not a
single download: on a closed network the climb would pass its checks, refresh
its lists, and stall on the very first package — after the first full backup,
hours in.

The apt configuration now proxies the download host as well. A global proxy is
still opt-in (`--proxy-all-apt`), because an internal Ubuntu mirror usually
must not go through it.

`proxy test` gained a matching rung. It probed the repository host and reported
a clean chain — a promise about package downloads it had never tested. It now
probes the download host through the same proxy and stops there when it cannot
reach it, because nothing later in the chain matters if the packages cannot
arrive.
